name: Clay tablet and reed stylus
tool: A cut reed pressed into wet clay
how: Scribes pressed the end of a reed into soft clay, leaving wedge-shaped marks (cuneiform). The tablet was dried or baked to keep the record.

name: Reed pen on papyrus
how: A reed was cut to a point or a brush end and dipped in black carbon ink made from soot and gum. Papyrus sheets were glued into long rolls.

name: Wax tablet and stylus
how: Letters were scratched into a layer of wax. To reuse the tablet, the flat end of the stylus smoothed the wax over again.

name: Brush and ink stick
how: An ink stick is rubbed with water on an ink stone to make fresh ink. The brush's softness lets the writer vary the line from hair-fine to thick.

name: Palm leaf and iron stylus
region: South and Southeast Asia (including Kerala and Tamil Nadu)
how: Palm leaves are dried and cut into long strips. A scribe scratches the letters into the leaf with an iron stylus. Soot or lamp-black mixed with oil is rubbed over the leaf and wiped off, so it stays only in the grooves. Strips are threaded on a cord through holes to make a book.

name: Birch bark and bone stylus
region: Novgorod and other northern Russian towns
how: Ordinary people scratched short letters, notes and lists onto strips of birch bark. Hundreds of these have been found in the soil of Novgorod.

name: Quill and iron-gall ink
how: A feather was cut to a point with a knife, giving a flexible nib. Ink was made from oak galls, iron salts and gum, and darkened as it dried on the page.

name: Steel dip pen
how: Cheap steel nibs let nearly everyone write and draw. The nib had to be dipped into an inkwell every few words.

name: Fountain pen
region: Europe, the United States and Asia
tool: Nib with a built-in ink reservoir
how: The pen carries its own ink and feeds it to the nib by capillary action. The nib is tipped with a hard metal so it keeps its shape.

name: Ballpoint pen
tool: Tiny ball in a socket, with oily ink
how: A small rolling ball picks up thick, quick-drying ink from a cartridge. It is cheap and leak-resistant, and it replaced the fountain pen for most everyday writing.
